## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of page fault handling, race avoidance, and lazy caching in OS kernels, focused on practical state management rather than theory.

## Key Concepts
- Page fault lifecycle and lazy loading
- Per-page state machine (INVALID, LOADING, VALID, DIRTY)
- Concurrency control via per-page locks and wait queues
- Disk I/O orchestration vs memory effects

## Code Example

```c
// Pseudo sketch of per-page state transitions
typedef enum { INVALID, LOADING, VALID, DIRTY } state_t;
struct page { state_t s; spinlock_t lock; wait_queue_t wq; };
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test correctness under many concurrent faults?
- How would you extend to handle multiple I/O devices and non-blocking fault handling?

Realistic multi-tenant I/O scheduling under contention; tests fairness, backpressure, and race handling.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant QoS quotas
- Lock-free enqueue/dequeue and CAS coordination
- Global arbitration with aging for fairness

- **NUMA awareness**: Huge page backing and node-local memory placement
